Labels are rule-based derivations from independent published sources (NASA FIRMS type, EOG VIIRS Nightfire flare sites, Maus et al. 2022 mining polygons, ESA WorldCover 2021), not field-verified ground truth. Test metrics measure agreement with those labels on unseen 0.5-degree blocks in a later year.

NASA derives FIRMS type 2 (static land source) from multi-year detection persistence. The model's history features measure related persistence, so part of the industrial/flare/mining signal is a proxy for how that label source was built. The without_history_features ablation quantifies this.
Maus et al. mining polygons include processing infrastructure, so smelters or steel works inside a mapped mining footprint are labelled mining_thermal_activity rather than industrial_fire.
gas_flare depends on the EOG VNF catalogue (156 Indian flare sites in 2023, 158 in 2024). A static source missing from it is labelled industrial_fire (type 2) or other_or_uncertain (type 3 offshore).
WorldCover is a 2021 map applied to 2023-2024 detections; land-cover change is not modelled. Shifting cultivation (jhum) in north-east India burns in tree cover and is labelled wildfire.

WorldCover footprint fractions are computed on the COG's first overview level (20 m) rather than the native 10 m, because of download bandwidth. On 3,000 real footprints the 20 m and 10 m fractions produced the same label 98.8% of the time (mean fraction difference 0.0098).
OSM context is a September 2026 Geofabrik snapshot applied to 2022-2024 detections.
Training uses standard-processing (archive) detections; live serving receives NRT detections, whose radiometry and geolocation can differ slightly.
VIIRS NOAA-21 context is available only from 2024-01-17 (NRT). 2023 training rows' cluster and history counts therefore lack a third VIIRS satellite that 2024 test rows and live production include.

The completeness gate is unchanged: a detection with no mapped industrial, power, oil/gas or mining OSM feature within 25 km cannot be classified in production, so such rows were excluded from training and test. Remote wildfires are under-represented as a result (see serving_gate).

The live database's history begins when ingestion began, so recurrence and FRP-baseline features start shallower in production than in training (which had up to two years of prior detections) until history accumulates.

The production dedup index {location.coordinates, detectedAt, satellite, instrument} is multikey on the coordinate array, so two distinct detections that share only a latitude or only a longitude in the same overpass collide. Loading the archive through it rejected about 0.3-0.4% of VIIRS rows and 0.6-1.1% of MODIS rows; training context inherits the same drops as production.
Detections come from FIRMS India country files (FIRMS's boundary); the live backend ingests a rectangular bounding box that includes neighbouring countries.
